sample_description: 2,453 U.S. adults from a Qualtrics online panel, quota-sampled to the U.S. adult population on gender, age and education (not a probability sample; no weights), fielded October-November 2015; respondents who failed two of three attention checks were removed before this file. Arm sizes are listed separately below. Each respondent was told they would read a short excerpt from an opinion article in USA Today, then read ONE excerpt of 70-150 words attributed to a fictitious 'Dr. Dave Wilson, a recognized international expert' (in public health, meteorology or earth science) about one of four topics: the flu, marijuana use, severe weather, or climate change. Every excerpt opens with the same kind of paragraph stating that recent research shows the problem is more dangerous and costly than believed and is raising everyone's insurance costs; in two of the three versions per topic a second paragraph follows in which he urges action and advocates a specific piece of legislation as a simple, inexpensive and effective response. Afterwards respondents rated the primary goal of the op-ed, whether he separated expert analysis from personal views, what motivated him, their impression of him on nine 8-point adjective pairs, and how controversial his research is. There were no pre-treatment attitude or trust measures.

credibility.question: 'Please indicate your impression of Dr. Wilson by choosing the appropriate number between the pairs of adjectives below.' 8-point bipolar items, scored so that HIGHER = MORE FAVOURABLE; mean of all 9 pairs (intelligent, concerned about society, competent, expert, sensitive, trustworthy, cares about society, sincere, honest); McCroskey & Teven source credibility

credibility_competence.question: 'Please indicate your impression of Dr. Wilson by choosing the appropriate number between the pairs of adjectives below.' 8-point bipolar items, scored so that HIGHER = MORE FAVOURABLE; COMPETENCE, mean of 3 pairs: not at all intelligent-extremely intelligent, not at all competent-extremely competent, not at all expert-extremely expert

credibility_goodwill.question: 'Please indicate your impression of Dr. Wilson by choosing the appropriate number between the pairs of adjectives below.' 8-point bipolar items, scored so that HIGHER = MORE FAVOURABLE; GOODWILL, mean of 3 pairs: isn't concerned about society at all-is concerned about society a great deal, not at all sensitive-extremely sensitive, doesn't care about society at all-cares about society a great deal

credibility_trustworthiness.question: 'Please indicate your impression of Dr. Wilson by choosing the appropriate number between the pairs of adjectives below.' 8-point bipolar items, scored so that HIGHER = MORE FAVOURABLE; TRUSTWORTHINESS, mean of 3 pairs: not at all trustworthy-extremely trustworthy, not at all sincere-extremely sincere, not at all honest-extremely honest

goal_impartial_information.question: 'The primary goal of Dr. Wilson's op-ed in USA Today was to provide impartial information about [topic]', 1 'Strongly disagree' - 7 'Strongly agree'

goal_persuade_action.question: 'The primary goal of Dr. Wilson's op-ed in USA Today was to persuade people to take action about [topic]', 1 'Strongly disagree' - 7 'Strongly agree'

separated_analysis_from_views.question: 'In his op-ed, Dr. Wilson clearly made an effort to separate his expert analysis of the scientific evidence from his personal views' (label truncated in the deposit after 'scientific'), 1 'Strongly disagree' - 7 'Strongly agree'

motive_scientific_evidence.question: 'Dr. Wilson's op-ed in USA Today was motivated by his evaluation of the scientific evidence on the issue of [topic]', 1 'Strongly disagree' - 7 'Strongly agree'

motive_personal_gain.question: 'Dr. Wilson's op-ed in USA Today was motivated by his desire for personal promotion and gain on the issue of [topic]', 1 'Strongly disagree' - 7 'Strongly agree'. HIGHER = MORE self-interested motive attributed (a message that works should move this DOWN or not at all)

motive_serve_public.question: 'Dr. Wilson's op-ed in USA Today was motivated by his desire to serve the public on the issue of [topic]', 1 'Strongly disagree' - 7 'Strongly agree'

motive_political_views.question: 'Dr. Wilson's op-ed in USA Today was motivated by his political views on the issue of [topic]', 1 'Strongly disagree' - 7 'Strongly agree'. HIGHER = MORE political motive attributed

research_controversial.question: 'Overall, how controversial do you believe Dr. Wilson's research in general is?' 1 'Not at all controversial' - 5 'Extremely controversial'. HIGHER = MORE controversial

moderators_unavailable.party: party identification was not asked; the closest item is 5-point ideology Q44 (v2 file only, joined by row position and verified on the nine Q19 items), carried above as the non-target moderator `ideology` (Very/Somewhat liberal -> Liberal; Moderate; Somewhat/Very conservative -> Conservative)
moderators_unavailable.education: Q48 has 5 levels (less than HS / HS graduate / some college or tech / college graduate / post graduate); the target's graduate-degree split is not recoverable, so it is carried raw as `education_raw` and not mapped
moderators_unavailable.race: Q49 Hispanic yes/no (carried as `hispanic`) and Q50_1-5 check-all-that-apply race boxes with 12 blanks and 50 multi-racial rows in v1; not carried, no clean single-level mapping

message_texts.Flu - information only:
Dr. Dave Wilson, a recognized international expert in the field of public health, recently published an op-ed in USA Today. In the article, he said:

“Evidence from recent scientific studies reveal that the flu is even more dangerous and costly than once believed. The flu contributes to pneumonia, bronchitis, fatigue, and even premature death. Moreover, since so many people are affected by the flu, it is increasing everyone's insurance costs."
message_texts.Flu - non-controversial solution (hand-w:

“Evidence from recent scientific studies reveal that the flu is even more dangerous and costly than once believed. The flu contributes to pneumonia, bronchitis, fatigue, and even premature death. Moreover, since so many people are affected by the flu, it is increasing everyone's insurance costs.

The flu threatens everyone and action should be urgently taken to reduce the risk. One effective approach for addressing the problem of the flu is to introduce legislation to post information signs about the link between hand washing and the flu in all restaurants and public buildings. My research, and research conducted by many other experts, suggests that this simple and inexpensive action is an effective way to protect Americans from the risks of the flu."

readme_claims: N = 2,453; 12 cells with counts flu 206/190/225, marijuana 213/199/205, severe weather 197/200/220, climate change 192/202/204
every row has exactly one non-missing column among Q3-Q14; column -> cell mapping reproduces the v2 Topic/Position with 0 disagreements
credibility = mean of Q19_1-9 with Q19_1/2/7/8 reversed as 9 - x; n = 2,452, M = 5.709, SD = 1.417, alpha = 0.913, identical to v2 Credibility

provenance.study_choice: single study (one paper, one deposit); the 4 topic x 3 position design is used whole. The within-topic INFORMATION-ONLY cell is the control for that topic's two advocacy cells (`control_strata` = topic), because the paper's estimand is the effect of appending an advocacy paragraph to an otherwise identical excerpt; a grand-mean control over four unrelated topics would confound topic with advocacy.
caveats: post-only design: no pre-treatment credibility, trust or attitude measure; the only baseline is the same-topic information-only cell, and there is no no-message control
the outcome is the credibility of ONE fictitious scientist after ONE op-ed excerpt, not trust in scientists as a group; the target's 12-item trust composite is a different object
each treatment arm is scored against its own topic's information-only cell (control_strata); the eight ATEs therefore have four different control groups of n ~ 192-213
only the three climate-change cells (n = 598) are on a climate topic; the other nine concern flu, marijuana and severe weather
the four 'reversed' items and the composites are ALREADY oriented high = favourable in the derived file - do not reverse again
credibility and its three 3-item subscales are the same 9 items, so those four rows per arm are not independent tests

the deposit's S1 questionnaire lists 8 adjective pairs and notes that a 7-point scale was rendered with 8 radio buttons; the data have 9 items, all 1-8, and the composite follows the authors' v2 Credibility
Q33 (how controversial is the proposed solution) was asked only in the two solution arms and is excluded: no control value exists
Qualtrics quota panel, 2015, no weights; no party identification and no income; ideology is a 5-point self-placement from the v2 file joined by position
the article's Tables 2-5 were corrected in 2019 (re-cleaned data); the printed M = 5.77 is from the erroneous set, the data give 5.71 - this adapter follows the data, not the article text
